prompt: Implement decode_rpc_chunks(chunks, max_fragment=16, max_record=32, eof=True) for RFC 5531 Section 11 record-marking framing only. chunks is a list of at most 100 pieces, each an even-length ASCII hexadecimal string (either case, no whitespace) encoding at most 1024 bytes. Empty pieces are harmless and do not signal EOF; eof is the separate Boolean end-of-input signal. Each call starts a fresh stream. Every four-byte unsigned network-order marker contains a high last-fragment bit and a low-31-bit payload length; marker bytes are not payload. Zero-length fragments are legal, including an empty final record; RPC body/argument validity is outside this framer. Concatenate fragment payloads until a last fragment completes its record. Preserve parser state across pieces, which can split markers/payloads or contain several records. max_fragment and max_record are integer policy limits (not bool), 0 through 4096, counting payload bytes; they are chosen implementation caps, not RFC-wide constants. At each complete marker, reject a length above max_fragment first, then a cumulative record length above max_record, before waiting for that payload or allocating its declared size. Return exactly {'records':[lowercase_complete_record_hex,...],'pending':bool,'error':None|'fragment-limit'|'record-limit'|'truncated'}. Stop at the first limit error, preserve earlier completed records and return pending=False. At ordinary end with eof=True, any incomplete marker, payload, or unfinished non-final record yields truncated/pending=False; publish no partial record. With eof=False and no error, pending=True exactly when some framing record is incomplete, even if its completed non-final fragments had zero payload; complete or empty input has pending=False. Reset cumulative size after each completed record. Do not mutate inputs or retain state across calls; this is byte framing, not a socket API or full RPC server.

Implement assemble_binary(frames, frame_cap, message_cap) for a decoded RFC 6455 binary-frame profile. frames is a list of at most 100 dictionaries {opcode:int,fin:bool,payload:hex_string}; opcodes are only 0 continuation,2 binary,8 Close,9 Ping,10 Pong. Payload is even-length ASCII hex without whitespace, either case, representing 0 through 512 bytes. Caps are integers, not bool, 0 through 4096, counting payload bytes. Wire/header decoding, masking, RSV/extensions, text/UTF-8 data messages and reserved opcodes are excluded. Every Close body is already semantically valid apart from the separately checked control FIN/size constraints: empty or a valid status plus valid UTF-8 reason, never a one-byte body. Return exactly {'messages':[lowercase_hex,...],'pongs':[lowercase_hex,...],'pending':lowercase_hex_or_None,'close_received':bool,'error':None_or_code}. Completed binary messages retain order; schedule a Pong with identical payload for each accepted Ping, without coalescing in this helper, and do not answer unsolicited Pongs. Controls neither contribute to nor reset an unfinished binary message. First reject payload length>frame_cap with frame_too_large. Next, for controls reject FIN=False or payload length>125 with invalid_control. For data, reject a new binary while a fragmented message exists (unexpected_binary) or a continuation without one (unexpected_continuation), then reject accumulated message bytes>message_cap (message_too_large). Equality at a cap is allowed. FIN completes the binary message and resets its accumulation. At ordinary end pending holds unfinished binary bytes, including an empty string for an active empty fragmented message; None means no pending message. On the first error preserve earlier messages/pongs, clear pending and return with close_received=False. On a valid Close, this selected local policy clears unfinished binary data, sets close_received=True, preserves earlier output and stops without processing later frames. It does not claim the TCP connection or full Close handshake completed; Close replies are outside this helper. Calls are fresh and inputs unchanged.

Implement coap_exchange(peer, mid, token, r_ms, events) for a bounded stateful RFC-7252 CON-request matching/rejection profile with retained known-Token state. peer is an opaque nonempty endpoint-identity string compared exactly; mid is an integer 0..65535; token is canonical lowercase hex for 0..8 token bytes, possibly empty. r_ms is the already-selected integer initial wait 2000..3000 milliseconds, corresponding to default ACK_TIMEOUT=2s and ACK_RANDOM_FACTOR=1.5. Send initially at time0; do not redraw jitter. With on-time processing and MAX_RETRANSMIT=4, nominal retries occur at R,3R,7R,15R and give-up at31R. events have nondecreasing integer at_ms in 0..246999, before the default exchange lifetime. A tick has kind='tick' and at_ms only; empty_ack also has peer/mid; piggyback and separate also have peer/mid/token. All inputs are already syntactically valid decoded messages; response events contain a final result accepted by the selected security/content/application policy once correlated. There is no wire parser, multicast, RST, stateless token-extension profile, response-CON ACK generation, or actual network. Return an initial snapshot and one after each event, each exactly {'transmissions':[integer_ms,...],'next_timeout':int_or_None,'message_failed':bool,'complete':bool}. A valid empty ACK matches peer+MID, cancels that message timer, and does not complete the application response. Piggybacked responses require peer+MID+Token; separate responses require peer+Token and can use a different MID. A matching separate response also cancels request retries if it precedes the empty ACK. Wrong correlation has no direct effect; advancing time can still trigger timers. Under this stateful whole-rejection profile, an unexpected piggybacked response is ignored rather than accepted as an ACK-only success. complete means acceptance of the matching final result, not durable business effects. message_failed records historical message-transmission give-up, not proof of nonexecution; retain request correlation for a later matching response within this trace, which can make complete=True without erasing message_failed. No independent application-response deadline is modeled. Process timers strictly before an event first. Process all listed events at an equal timestamp in order before any timer at that exact timestamp; the snapshot for the last event at that timestamp includes the subsequent equal-time timer processing, and earlier snapshots do not. Once complete, later messages cannot restart the exchange. Calls are independent; inputs and historical snapshots remain unchanged.

Implement simulate_invocations(initial_counter, commands), a deterministic logical atomic-ledger simulation, not a physical storage/durability experiment. initial_counter is an integer, not bool, in [-1000000,1000000]; commands has at most100 entries. Every identifier is a nonempty 1..32-character ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_-] string, compared case-sensitively. The complete invocation key is the ordered tuple (client,incarnation,request). Begin attempt IDs are globally unique within a call. Commands have exactly these schemas: {'op':'begin','attempt':id,'client':id,'incarnation':id,'request':id,'delta':int}, with delta in[-1000,1000]; {'op':'commit','attempt':id,'reply':bool}; {'op':'crash'}; {'op':'evict','client':id,'incarnation':id,'request':id}. A commit may name an absent attempt. Initial retained records and volatile pending attempts are empty. begin only stages key/delta, freezing no duplicate decision and applying no effect. Each commit consumes the pending attempt and atomically checks the CURRENT retained record: absent record adds delta to the counter and stores {delta,result:new_counter}, status committed; same key/delta changes no state and uses the ORIGINAL stored result, status replayed; same key with different delta changes neither counter nor record, status conflict. Absent attempt gives status missing. For committed/replayed, reply=True exposes the integer result and reply=False suppresses it to None without rollback. Conflict/missing have reply=None. Consumed attempts remain absent even after replay/conflict. crash discards all pending attempts but preserves counter and retained records under the declared fault model. evict removes exactly its retained key if present, without changing counter or pending attempts; later retry may then execute again. No automatic expiry/eviction. Return exactly {'counter':int,'records':[{'key':[client,incarnation,request],'delta':int,'result':int}], 'pending':[{'attempt':id,'key':[...],'delta':int}], 'events':list}. Sort records by complete key and pending by attempt. Event order follows commands: begin gives {op:'begin',attempt,status:'pending'}; commit gives {op:'commit',attempt,status:'committed'|'replayed'|'conflict'|'missing',reply:int_or_None}; crash gives {op:'crash',discarded:[sorted_pending_attempt_ids]}; evict gives {op:'evict',key:[...],removed:bool}. This event list exposes simulator/server state, not the client's knowledge after a lost reply. Calls are fresh and inputs unchanged; no validation beyond the stated input domain is needed.

Implement heartbeat_trace(events), a declared one-outstanding-probe detector using exact connection/probe correlation. It reports suspicion, never proof of a crash or whole-service health. Each event has nonnegative integer at (abstract clock ticks), in nondecreasing order. start events contain kind='start', at, connection, probe, timeout (positive integer); pong contains kind='pong', at, connection, probe; tick contains kind='tick', at only. Connection/probe identifiers are nonempty ASCII strings compared case-sensitively. Each (connection,probe) start pair is unique within the trace; the same probe string may appear on a different connection. Initial pending=None and suspected=False. BEFORE every event, if an outstanding deadline<=at, mark suspected=True and clear that pending probe. Then start replaces any still-pending probe and cancels its old timer, setting {connection,probe,deadline:at+timeout}; starting alone never clears suspicion. A Pong is accepted only when a still-pending probe has exactly both identifiers; acceptance clears suspicion and cancels that timer. Wrong, unsolicited or expired Pongs have no direct effect. Thus a Pong exactly at the deadline loses to expiry, and an old probe expiring at/before a replacement start sets suspicion before the new probe begins. tick only advances time. Return a snapshot after every event with exactly {'suspected':bool,'pending':None_or_{connection,probe,deadline:int},'pong_accepted':None_or_bool}. For start/tick pong_accepted=None; for every pong it records actual acceptance. A fresh timely reply can clear suspicion from an earlier probe. No actual network, WebSocket frame parsing, remote cancellation or application-health inference is modeled. Inputs and historical snapshot values remain unchanged and each call starts fresh.
